_comment: The vocabulary of the fault surface (issue #24). One definition of the six faults a job can be made to suffer on demand; the control plane (orchestrator and fake provider) and the trainer image both read this file, so the two sides cannot drift about what a fault is called, which side makes it real, or which parameters it takes. A value two components must agree on is defined once and read, never retyped. `code` is present only where the fault's run carries its own coded result (oom and divergence); the other four fail through the platform's ordinary machinery (the stall detector, a missing result document, teardown) and are named by the run's history instead. `params` is the parameter vocabulary each fault accepts; a parameter outside it is refused loudly rather than silently dropped.

faults.name: divergence
faults.description: drive the loss to a meaningless value

faults.name: machine_silent
faults.description: make the machine go silent without ending

faults.name: orphan
faults.description: leave a machine running with no job that owns it

faults.name: destroy_refused
faults.description: make the provider refuse a destroy
